graph.summary: Cetuximab → Epidermal growth factor receptor → MAPK cascade → cell population proliferation → Colorectal Cancer

evidence.snippet: the blocking of EGFR ligand binding using antibodies directed against the extracellular domain of the receptor (e.g., cetuximab)
evidence.explanation: Cetuximab is an antibody directed against the extracellular ligand-binding domain of EGFR.

paper.title: The role of EGFR inhibition in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.

evidence.snippet: the effect of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) blockade on cell survival and on downstream signalling pathways using the monoclonal antibody cetuximab
evidence.explanation: Cetuximab produces EGFR blockade affecting downstream signalling pathways in colon cancer cell lines.

paper.title: Epidermal growth factor receptor status and persistent activation of Akt and p44/42 MAPK pathways correlate with the effect of cetuximab in head and neck and colon cancer cell lines.
paper.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology

evidence.snippet: It activates the downstream signal pathway AKT-MTOR and RAS-MAPK, increases proliferation, migration, and invasion
evidence.explanation: EGFR activation drives the downstream RAS-MAPK signaling pathway in colorectal cancer cells.

paper.title: Morphine promotes tumorigenesis and cetuximab resistance via EGFR signaling activation in human colorectal cancer.

evidence.snippet: Reduced NF1 expression permitted sustained signaling through the MAPK pathway to promote cell proliferation in the presence of EGFR inhibition
evidence.explanation: Signaling through the MAPK pathway promotes cell proliferation in colorectal cancer cells.

paper.title: Inactivation of NF1 Promotes Resistance to EGFR Inhibition in KRAS/NRAS/BRAFV600 -Wild-Type Colorectal Cancer.

evidence.snippet: treatment with morphine could activate MOR and lead to the promotion of proliferation, migration, and invasion in HCT116 and DLD1 colorectal cancer (CRC) cells
evidence.explanation: Proliferation drives the malignant phenotype of colorectal cancer cells.

paper.title: Morphine promotes tumorigenesis and cetuximab resistance via EGFR signaling activation in human colorectal cancer.

evidence.snippet: Anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies such as cetuximab (CTX) have been approved for the treatment of various malignancies, including colorectal cancer (CRC) with wild-type KRAS
evidence.explanation: Cetuximab is an approved anti-EGFR antibody for the treatment of colorectal cancer.

paper.title: Combination therapy with zoledronic acid and cetuximab effectively suppresses growth of colorectal cancer cells regardless of KRAS status.
